arxiv-1608-07935.creator: Jing Wang, Guo-Zhu Liu, Dmitry V. Efremov, Jeroen van den Brink
arxiv-1608-07935.description: Abstract The competition among superconductivity, stripe-type magnetic order, and a new type of C 4 C_{4} symmetric magnetic order in Ba 1 − x ​ K x ​ Fe 2 ​ As 2 \mathrm{Ba_{1-x}K_{x}Fe_{2}As_{2}} is theoretically studied, focusing on its impact on the global phase diagram.

arxiv-1812-08524.description: Abstract We study the quasi-two-body decays B → D ∗ ​ h → D ​ π ​ h B\to D^{*}h\to D\pi h with h = ( π , K ) h=(\pi,K) in the perturbative QCD approach and focus on the virtual contributions from the off-shell D ∗ ​ ( 2007 ) 0 D^{\ast}(2007)^{0} and D ∗ ​ ( 2010 )

arxiv-2004-10042.title: A Novel Graphic Bending Transformation on Benchmark C. Liu and F. Sun——Contribute equally to this article.
arxiv-2004-10042.creator: Chunxiuzi Liu 1 , Fengyang Sun 1 , Qingrui Ni 1 , Lin Wang 1,∗ , Bo Yang 1,2
arxiv-2004-10042.description: Abstract Classical benchmark problems utilize multiple transformation techniques to increase optimization difficulty, e.g., shift for anti centering effect and rotation for anti dimension sensitivity. Despite testing the transformation invariance, however, such operations do not really change the landscape’s “shape”, but rather than change the “view point”.

arxiv-2111-06406.title: From Pebbles and Planetesimals to Planets and Dust: the Protoplanetary Disk–Debris Disk Connection Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2111-06406.creator: Joan R. Najita, Scott J. Kenyon, Benjamin C. Bromley
arxiv-2111-06406.description: Abstract The similar orbital distances and detection rates of debris disks and the prominent rings observed in protoplanetary disks suggest a potential connection between these structures. We explore this connection with new calculations that follow the evolution of rings of pebbles and planetesimals as they grow into planets and generate dusty debris.

arxiv-2112-07820.title: Value Retrieval with Arbitrary Queries for Form-like Documents
arxiv-2112-07820.creator: Mingfei Gao, Le Xue, Chetan Ramaiah, Chen Xing, Ran Xu, Caiming Xiong Salesforce Research, Palo Alto, USA {mingfei.gao, lxue, cramaiah, cxing, ran.xu, cxiong}@salesforce.com
arxiv-2112-07820.description: Abstract We propose value retrieval with arbitrary queries for form-like documents to reduce human effort of processing forms. Unlike previous methods that only address a fixed set of field items, our method predicts target value for an arbitrary query based on the understanding of the layout and semantics of a form.

arxiv-2401-01845.title: Hille’s theorem for Bochner integrals of functions with values in locally convex spaces
arxiv-2401-01845.creator: T. J. Sullivan
arxiv-2401-01845.description: Abstract Abstract. Hille’s theorem is a powerful classical result in vector measure theory. It asserts that the application of a closed, unbounded linear operator commutes with strong/Bochner integration of functions taking values in a Banach space. This note shows that Hille’s theorem also holds in the setting of complete locally convex spaces. Keywords.

arxiv-2402-07888.title: Statistical analysis of the fluctuations of an initial-state model with independently distributed hot spots
arxiv-2402-07888.creator: Nicolas Borghini, Hendrik Roch, Alicia Schütte
arxiv-2402-07888.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Borghini, Hendrik Roch, Alicia Schütte. We determine the uncorrelated modes that characterize the fluctuations in a semi-realistic model for the initial state of high-energy nuclear collisions, consisting of hot spots whose positions are distributed independently.

arxiv-2408-12637.title: Building and better understanding vision-language models: insights and future directions
arxiv-2408-12637.creator: Hugo Laurençon, Andrés Marafioti, Victor Sanh, Léo Tronchon *
arxiv-2408-12637.description: Abstract The field of vision-language models (VLMs), which take images and texts as inputs and output texts, is rapidly evolving and has yet to reach consensus on several key aspects of the development pipeline, including data, architecture, and training methods. This paper can be seen as a tutorial for building a VLM.

arxiv-2502-16102.title: Some spectral results for certain positive operators in Hilbert Spaces
arxiv-2502-16102.creator: Rashid A, P Sam Johnson
arxiv-2502-16102.description: Abstract This paper investigates spectral properties of certain classes of positive operators originated from different matrices appeared in linear complementarity problem. These positive operators play a crucial role in various areas of mathematics and its applications, including operator theory, functional analysis, and quantum mechanics.

arxiv-2502-20653.title: Dataset Distillation with Neural Characteristic Function: A Minmax Perspective
arxiv-2502-20653.creator: Shaobo Wang, Yicun Yang, Zhiyuan Liu, Chenghao Sun, Xuming Hu, Conghui He, Linfeng Zhang
arxiv-2502-20653.description: Abstract Dataset distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for reducing data requirements in deep learning. Among various methods, distribution matching-based approaches stand out for their balance of computational efficiency and strong performance. However, existing distance metrics used in distribution matching often fail to accurately capture distributional differences, leading to unreliable measures of discrepancy.

arxiv-2505-19531.title: Minimalist Softmax Attention Provably Learns Constrained Boolean Functions
arxiv-2505-19531.creator: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu and Xiwen Zhang ∗ and Maojiang Su and Zhao Song and Han Liu
arxiv-2505-19531.description: Abstract We study the computational limits of learning k k -bit Boolean functions (specifically, AND \mathrm{AND} , OR \mathrm{OR} , and their noisy variants), using a minimalist single-head softmax-attention mechanism, where k = Θ ⁡ ( d ) k=\Theta(d) relevant bits are selected from d d inputs.

arxiv-2506-06819.title: A Novel Fine Spectral Structure of Solar Radio Bursts with Periodic Beaded Stripes Observed by CBSm of CMP-II
arxiv-2506-06819.creator: Chuanyang Li, Yao Chen, Bing Wang, Ze Zhong, Baolin Tan, Zongjun Ning, Hao Ning, Xiangliang Kong, Shuwang Chang, Yanke Tang, Ning Gai, Li Deng, Jingye Yan, Fabao Yan
arxiv-2506-06819.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chuanyang Li, Yao Chen, Bing Wang, Ze Zhong, Baolin Tan, Zongjun Ning, Hao Ning, Xiangliang Kong, Shuwang Chang, Yanke Tang, Ning Gai, Li Deng, Jingye Yan, Fabao Yan. A novel fine spectral structure in solar radio bursts has been discovered using the Chashan broadband solar radio spectrometer at meter wavelengths (CBSm), an instrument of the Chinese Meridian Project-Phase II (CMP-II).

arxiv-2507-00863.title: REAP-T: A MATLAB Toolbox for Implementing Robust-to-Early Termination Model Predictive Control
arxiv-2507-00863.creator: Mohsen Amiri and Mehdi Hosseinzadeh
arxiv-2507-00863.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohsen Amiri and Mehdi Hosseinzadeh. This paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for implementing robust-to-early termination model predictive control, abbreviated as REAP, which is designed to ensure a sub-optimal yet feasible solution when MPC computations are prematurely terminated due to limited computational resources. Named REAP-T, this toolbox is a comprehensive, user-friendly, and modular platform that enables users to explore, analyze, and customize various components of REAP for their specific applications.

arxiv-2511-01281.title: Mathematical Foundations and Backpropagation from First Principles: A Step-by-Step Guide
arxiv-2511-01281.creator: Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar
arxiv-2511-01281.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar. Particle Filter Made Simple: A Step-by-Step Beginner-friendly Guide

Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar

Arizona State University

sdhayalk@asu.edu

Abstract

The particle filter is a powerful framework for estimating hidden states in dynamic systems where uncertainty, noise, and nonlinearity dominate. This mini-book offers a clear and structured introduction to the core ideas behind particle filters—how they represent uncertainty through random samples, update beliefs using observations, and maintain robustness where linear or Gaussian assumptions fail.

arxiv-2601-11042.title: Spectral Characterization and Mitigation of Sequential Knowledge Editing Collapse
arxiv-2601-11042.creator: Chi Zhang, Mengqi Zhang, Xiaotian Ye, Runxi Cheng, Zisheng Zhou, Ying Zhou, Pengjie Ren, Zhumin Chen
arxiv-2601-11042.description: Abstract Sequential knowledge editing in large language models often causes catastrophic collapse of the model’s general abilities, especially for parameter-modifying methods. Existing approaches mitigate this issue through heuristic constraints on parameter updates, yet the mechanisms underlying such degradation remain insufficiently understood.

britannica-1911-caucasia.title: Caucasia (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-caucasia.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-caucasia.description: Article 'Caucasia' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 5), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. (i.) The plains of Northern Caucasia, which include most of the provinces of Kubañ and Terek and of the government of Stavropol, slope gently downwards from the foot of the Caucasus range towards the Kuma-Manych depression. It is only in their centre that they reach altitudes of as much as 2000–2500 ft.

pmc-10533491.title: Shifts in isoform usage underlie transcriptional differences in regulatory T cells in type 1 diabetes
pmc-10533491.creator: Jeremy R B Newman, S Alice Long, Cate Speake, Carla J Greenbaum, Karen Cerosaletti, Stephen S Rich, Suna Onengut-Gumuscu, Lauren M McIntyre, Jane H Buckner, Patrick Concannon
pmc-10533491.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Genome-wide association studies have identified numerous loci with allelic associations to Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) risk. Most disease-associated variants are enriched in regulatory sequences active in lymphoid cell types, suggesting that lymphocyte gene expression is altered in T1D. Here we assay gene expression between T1D cases and healthy controls in two autoimmunity-relevant lymphocyte cell types, memory CD4+/CD25+ regulatory T cells (Treg) and memory CD4+/CD25- T cells, using a splicing event-based approach to characterize tissue-specific transcriptomes.
